what_its_for: Metreleptin is used to treat complications caused by leptin deficiency in adults and children with generalized lipodystrophy — a rare condition where the body lacks fat tissue. It works by replacing a hormone called leptin that your body is not making enough of. This hormone helps control hunger, metabolism, and blood sugar levels.
how_to_take: Metreleptin is given as a shot (injection) under the skin (subcutaneous injection), once a day. You will inject it into your stomach area (abdomen), upper thigh, or upper arm. Rotate (change) the injection site each day to avoid skin irritation. Your doctor or nurse will show you exactly how to prepare and give the injection. Always use a new needle and syringe for each injection. Never share your needles, syringes, or medicine with anyone else.
dosing: Your dose is based on your body weight and will be determined by your doctor. The usual starting dose for adults and children weighing more than 40 kg (about 88 lbs) is 2.5 mg once daily. For those weighing 40 kg or less, the starting dose is usually 0.06 mg per kg of body weight once daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose over time based on how your body responds. Always follow your doctor's exact dosing instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store unopened vials of metreleptin in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze metreleptin — throw it away if it has been frozen. Once you mix (reconstitute) the medicine with the supplied diluent (mixing liquid), you must use it right away or store it in the refrigerator and use it within 3 days. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used needles and syringes in an approved sharps disposal container — never throw them in the regular trash.
what_to_avoid: Do not use metreleptin if you are allergic to it or any of its ingredients. Avoid sharing needles, syringes, or vials with other people. Do not inject into skin that is red, irritated, bruised, or scarred. Talk to your doctor before taking any new medicines, vitamins, or supplements, as metreleptin can affect blood sugar levels and may change how other medicines — especially blood sugar medicines like insulin — work in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, rash, trouble breathing, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat; signs of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) such as shaking, sweating, fast heartbeat, dizziness, or confusion; signs of infection at the injection site such as redness, swelling, warmth, or pus; unexpected weight gain or changes in appetite; signs of lymphoma (a type of cancer) such as swollen lymph nodes, night sweats, or unexplained weight loss; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: It may take several weeks to months before you notice the full benefits of metreleptin. Many patients begin to see improvements in blood sugar (glucose) control and triglyceride (fat) levels within a few weeks. Some symptoms like hunger and metabolism improvements may take longer. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of metreleptin during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. Children: Metreleptin can be used in children with generalized lipodystrophy, but dosing is based on weight and will be carefully managed by your doctor. Elderly: There is limited information on the use of metreleptin in older adults. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or Liver Problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as this may affect how your body handles the medication.
